simple.meaning: אַלְמֻגִּים (ʼalmuggîym) is a Hebrew object word meaning “almug (i.e. probably sandle-wood) sticks.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at 1 Kings 10:11. The surrounding context includes kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אַלְמֻגִּים (H484) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: אַלְמֻגִּים (ʼalmuggîym) / H484 is traced through 1 Kings 10:11, 1 Kings 10:12 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.full: H484. almuggim אַלְמֻגִּים noun [masculine] plural id. אַלְמֻגִּים עֲצֵי 1Kin 10:11-12 , (from Ophir); ׳ע ׳הָא 10:12 .
definitions.rootNote: probably of foreign derivation (used thus only in the plural);

occurrences.englishText: The fleet of Hiram that brought gold from Ophir, also brought in from Ophir great quantities of almug trees* possibly an Indian sandalwood, with nice grain and a pleasant scent, and good for woodworking and precious stones.
The king made of the almug trees pillars for Yahweh’s house, and for the king’s house, harps also and stringed instruments for the singers; no such almug trees came or were seen, to this day.
